about.title: Personal Injury Help in Palmdale, California
about.longDescription: Palmdale sits at the high-desert edge of Los Angeles County, and its wide boulevards carry a lot of traffic between the Antelope Valley and the rest of the region. In 2025, the city recorded 815 injury collisions, with 1,231 people hurt and 14 lives lost. Public records show the heaviest collision counts along Palmdale Boulevard, Rancho Vista Boulevard, Avenue S, and Sierra Highway, and reports tend to rise on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. Those are simply counts, but each one represents a person whose week did not go as planned. If you were injured in a crash, a fall, a bite, or another incident someone else caused, you may be weighing whether to talk to a lawyer at all. We exist to make that first step simpler. We handle personal injury cases and work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. There is no charge to reach out, no obligation to hire us, and no pressure. You ask questions, get straight answers, and decide what comes next on your own timeline.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Palmdale Claim

items.title: The clock runs two years, sometimes less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to start early.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your case
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame but not eliminated.

items.title: No statutory ceiling on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as physical pain or emotional distress. What you went through can be fully considered.

items.title: Contingency fees, no upfront cost
items.desc: We are paid only if there is a recovery. You do not write a check to get started, and you pay us nothing unless your case results in compensation.

items.question: Where do collisions in Palmdale tend to happen?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the highest counts in Palmdale fall along Palmdale Boulevard, Rancho Vista Boulevard, Avenue S, and Sierra Highway. Reports also tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral record counts reflecting traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular street.

items.question: Do you charge me anything?
items.answer: No. We handle your case on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You pay us nothing at any point.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. If a government entity such as a city or transit agency is involved, you may need to file a claim within six months. Because the deadline depends on the facts, it is wise to ask an attorney about your specific situation soon.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover even if you share some responsibility. Your compensation is reduced in proportion to your percentage of fault rather than wiped out. We can help explain how that might apply to what happened to you.

items.question: What happens after I reach out?
items.answer: You share the basics of what happened, and we review your situation and explain your options. You are never obligated to hire us, and you decide how to proceed.
